topics.title: API Integration (Fetch, POST & PHP/MySQL)
topics.content:
React applications communicate with backend servers using standard HTTP requests. We fetch data using the native browser fetch() API inside a useEffect hook:

// Fetching data (GET)
useEffect(() => {
  fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
    .then(res => res.json())
    .then(data => setData(data));
}, []);

Sending Data (POST): We specify the method, headers, and body:

fetch('https://api.example.com/submit', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
});

PHP/MySQL Integration: In typical academic stacks, a PHP script queries MySQL and outputs JSON using echo json_encode($result); after configuring CORS headers: header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *");.
topics.interviewTip: When asked how a frontend SPA communicates with a server, emphasize that SPAs run entirely in the browser and use **Asynchronous HTTP Requests (AJAX)** via Fetch API or Axios. Explain that the backend is a separate API that handles database interactions and returns JSON data.

topics.title: AngularJS Introduction & Architecture
topics.content:
AngularJS: A legacy JavaScript framework developed by Google (v1.x) that extends HTML with custom attributes (directives) and binds data to HTML expressions.

MVC Architecture in AngularJS:

  • Model: The data in the application (stored as properties on the $scope object).
  • View: The HTML template that displays the data.
  • Controller: JavaScript functions that contain the business logic, modifying model data.

topics.title: Setting Up AngularJS & Your First App
topics.content:
AngularJS is loaded via a script tag. To initialize an AngularJS application, we use the ng-app directive. The ng-controller directive attaches a controller to the view:

<script src="https://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/angularjs/1.8.2/angular.min.js"></script>

<div ng-app="myApp" ng-controller="myCtrl">
  <p>Hello {{name}}</p>
</div>

In JavaScript, the module and controller are declared as:

const app = angular.module('myApp', []);
app.controller('myCtrl', function($scope) {
  $scope.name = 'Aritra';
});

topics.title: AngularJS Expressions & Object Binding
topics.content:
Expressions: Written inside double braces {{ expression }}. They act like placeholders that print variable values or evaluate basic equations. AngularJS supports:

  • Number expressions: {{ 5 + 5 }}
  • String expressions: {{ firstName + ' ' + lastName }}
  • Object expressions: {{ user.age }}
  • Array expressions: {{ items[2] }}

topics.title: Two-Way Data Binding
topics.content:
Unlike React (which uses one-way data binding), AngularJS features automatic **Two-Way Data Binding**. It synchronizes model and view: when model data changes, the view is updated, and when user inputs change in the view, the model data is updated automatically.

This is achieved using the ng-model directive on form elements: 

<input ng-model="name" />
<h1>Hello {{name}}</h1>

practiceQuestions.question: Write a React code snippet that fetches data from an API when the component mounts.
What is AngularJS and what architecture does it follow?
practiceQuestions.answer: AngularJS is a structural JavaScript framework for dynamic web apps. It extends HTML using attributes called directives. It follows the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architecture, where `$scope` holds the model data, HTML templates represent the view, and JavaScript functions manage the controllers.

practiceQuestions.question: Explain the difference between Data Binding in React and AngularJS.
practiceQuestions.answer: React features one-way data binding, where data flows in a single direction (state updates trigger re-renders, and updates from inputs must be handled manually via events). AngularJS features automatic two-way data binding using the `ng-model` directive, meaning changes in the input automatically update the model, and changes in the model automatically update the UI.

practiceQuestions.question: What are AngularJS expressions? List four types of expressions with examples.
practiceQuestions.answer:
AngularJS expressions are code blocks placed inside double braces `{{ }}` that display model data. Types:
(1) Number: `{{ quantity * cost }}`
(2) String: `{{ name }}`
(3) Object: `{{ student.roll }}`
(4) Array: `{{ scores[0] }}`

mcqs.question: Where should you place API data-fetching operations in a React functional component?
options: Inside a useEffect hook with an empty dependency array
mcqs.explanation: useEffect with a dependency array of `[]` runs exactly once after the component mounts, making it the correct location to fetch external data.

mcqs.question: Which HTTP method should be configured in the Fetch API options to submit data to a database?
mcqs.explanation: POST is the standard HTTP method used to send user payload data to backends to create or write resource records.

mcqs.question: To connect a frontend app to a PHP script on a different domain, which header must be set in the PHP script?
mcqs.explanation: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) security rules require that the server declare allowed origins via the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header.

mcqs.question: What architectural pattern is followed by AngularJS?
mcqs.explanation: AngularJS organizes applications using the MVC pattern (or Model-View-Whatever MVW).

mcqs.question: Which directive is mandatory to bootstrap and initialize an AngularJS application?
mcqs.explanation: The `ng-app` directive designates the root element of an AngularJS application and triggers the bootstrap process.

mcqs.question: How are AngularJS expressions written in HTML templates?
mcqs.explanation: AngularJS parses double curly braces `{{ }}` to evaluate expressions and bind dynamic output.

mcqs.question: Which AngularJS directive establishes automatic two-way data binding on form inputs?
mcqs.explanation: The `ng-model` directive binds the value of HTML controls (input, select, textarea) to application data in the scope.

mcqs.question: What is the role of the $scope object in AngularJS?
options: It acts as the glue (context) between the controller and the view, holding the model data
mcqs.explanation: The `$scope` object holds properties and functions that are accessible in both the controller and the view template.

mcqs.question: How does data binding in React differ from AngularJS?
options: React has two-way binding, AngularJS has one-way binding
React has one-way binding, AngularJS has two-way binding
Both have automatic two-way binding by default
mcqs.explanation: React enforces unidirectional (one-way) data flow. AngularJS features automatic bidirectional (two-way) data binding.

mcqs.question: In AngularJS, how do you define an application module in a JavaScript file?
mcqs.explanation: The syntax `angular.module('moduleName', [dependencies])` is the correct API to create a new module.
